search_strategy: Three-tier, keyword-driven rather than exhaustive. (1) Gitea: issue-title keyword search (0 hits, dead end -- line 1073-1083) -- the record wasn't in issues. (2) Mattermost: authenticated via the API (line 3150), listed all 12 channels, then ran ~25 sequential keyword searches ('EncodingReport','window_start','last_report','dropped_indices','to_jsonl_lines','FIREWORKS_BYTES_PER_TOKEN', 'retained_prompt_tokens','num_messages','minimum is 16', etc, lines 3406-5598), each returning message id/channel/timestamp/snippet. This found the great majority of chat remarks but missed any remark whose wording didn't overlap a queried term (14 chat/wiki misses share this cause). (3) Wiki: listed all ~165 pages via /api/pages, hand-selected 10 whose titles looked relevant (132,135,137,142,144,145,149,153,155,156) out of 15 that actually carried remarks, fetched each whole with its comments (line 1328-1377), then read most of them turn-by-turn in a chunked renderer -- but 3 of the 10 fetched pages' comment files (c135,c137,c142) were only ever hit by one narrow combined grep and never opened directly, and 3 candidate pages (86,154,197) were never fetched. (4) Mail: dumped the entire IMAP mailbox (all 153 messages) to a single file and read/grepped it, which is the most exhaustive of the three surfaces -- 12 of 13 mail remarks were found this way, only l13 (whose content duplicates the already-found l6 thread) slipped through. No truncation or crashed helper script hurt this run; two early python script bugs (AttributeError on comments field, an IMAP SEARCH syntax error) were self-corrected within one turn each.
end_reason: Not applicable -- the run completed normally: all 7 facts scored 1, CI green, pushed and deployed (provenance.pushed=1, provenance.ci_green=1, provenance.deployed=1, suite_ok=1). No failing-test traces in the pointer sheet.
notable: Search strategy was three-tier and effective: Mattermost via keyword search API (queries like 'EncodingReport','window_start','dropped_indices' -- line 3406-5598), mail via a full IMAP dump of all 153 messages to /tmp/allmail.txt read sequentially (line 4663-4712), wiki via selecting 10 of 15 candidate pages by title relevance and fetching each whole with comments (line 1328-1377).

3 wiki pages carrying remarks were never fetched at all: page 154 (viewer-dataset-download-export-format-notes-pr-652, g9.r1.l-fw-2), page 197 (weekly-notes-week-of-mar-31, g9.r2.l11), page 86 (weekly-sync-notes-week-of-jun-23-batch-mode, g9.r2.l5) -- all three were visible in the /api/pages listing the agent printed but not selected for the fetch.py run. None of the three were the sole carrier of a graded fact.

3 comment files were rendered (c135.md, c137.md, c142.md) but never individually opened -- only one combined grep for the term 'encoding' was run across all ten pages' rendered files (line 2955), which missed g9.r2.l8, g9.r2.l14, and g9.r1.say24 because their wording doesn't contain 'encoding'. This is a near-miss pattern (fetched-but-unread) distinct from the never-fetched pages.

8 chat remarks (g9.r1.l-rule-3, l-fail-4, l-fw-4, l-fail-1, fix28, g9.r2.l16, l12) were never surfaced because the agent's Mattermost queries never included their distinctive wording ('part credit', 'forty thousand', 'qqq', 'swallowd', 'assistant header', 'windowed came back as nine') -- the agent relied on a handful of technical-term searches rather than dumping channels/days whole.

Despite 14 of 57 remarks (25%) never surfacing, every graded fact scored 1 because the plant's redundancy held: each subconclusion had 3-5 independent carriers and at least 2-3 were found for every fact (see passed_facts).

The shipped code (verified from the raw tool-call keystrokes in the full rollout JSON, not just the truncated terminal echo) matches the answer key field-for-field: EncodingReport is @dataclass(frozen=True) with the exact field order/defaults; MIN_RETAINED_PROMPT_TOKENS=16 and FIREWORKS_BYTES_PER_TOKEN=3 are named constants; to_tinker_datum's docstring states verbatim 'This method never touches last_report; a single datum has no batch to be counted into.'
